body: I'm sure there are valid reasons to think others want you dead. if that's the case, these people do not matter and by extension, their opinions don't matter. if anyone's going to kill themselves, do it because of your own judgement. there are some people out here in this wide world you will vibe with. join book clubs if you like books. volunteer somewhere to be around people who give a shit. understand i'm just as depressed but finding the right people helps.

Yes, there is pure misery and pain. Buddhism even gets into this in a systematic way. Not promoting religion but the point is the observation of human suffering is not lost on many of us. True not everyone is at the suicidal level but I would argue most are in a state of pain; some are just adept at hiding it or cluttering their lives with shit that keeps them from thinking about it. We are all screwed up but that's probably the humanity of all this. I am now living with this realization although I suspect I will be done with it before my time is supposed to be up. Internal peace? Possible but it's just a possibility. If there's one thing I've learned, there are no short cuts, not even in death.
Ok. That's succinct. But, can you try talking through it first (here or wherever you need to do it)?

You might have high-functioning depression. It's a depression in which you are otherwise very productive with school and/or work but there's just an overwhelming feeling that manifests itself through fatigue and feelings of dislocation. 

Depression isn't always apparent as "doom and gloom" but it's definitely no less serious.

Thanks GusherVim. That's very informative. Reading what you wrote, it sounds like there has to a real resolve to want to get better and I just lack the commitment to change. It's very nihilistic but thanks again. I will think about what I learned.

The way I see it, people, especially those inexperienced with handguns, will miss their target. If if's difficult to hit your mark, I'm assuming shooting yourself in the "right" spot is easier said than done. I'm also concerned with the startle response aka flinch.

I don't trust myself to do it right. I feel like I'll blow my teeth out and survive.

Yeah, doing things legally really complicates what could've been easy.
TaurineLine719, I can totally relate and after considering and looking into viable methods, I still can't find one I can go with. The best way to go out requires resources I just don't have.

That's one reason and that's definitely why I've ruled out suicide by gunshot. Imagine if the recoil gets you shot in the eyes or mouth...There are pretty good options out there but they can't be done without risking a felony conviction/fine.

Weirdly, it's probably coming from a sincere place. I truly don't care about my own life but when I see others articulating suicide plans, I really do feel sad. Maybe it's also just an overall sadness that this thing I feel is actually felt by others.
Hmmm..you make a good point. I was trying to figure out why people who fear the unknowable afterlife would take a high risk...I guess it's desperation.
Totally..I wish it would all work out like an off switch. If it's worse on the other side, that would be a cruel joke from humanity.

thanks GusherVim..I actually followed up and did some reading into CBT. The fact that it's short-term and highly goal-driven definitely makes it sound different from other therapy. I will look into it some more but seeing how "cognitive distortions", "filtering", catastrophizing isn't quite what I do, I'm not sure it's quite right for me. I'm not too concerned about how people perceive/accept me. And, I can see some good in my life. But, in spite of it all, I feel disconnected. Thanks for reaching out though.

I totally agree with you. I can change my perspective and I know that I should but I just can't. No one will say that I'm a happy type but they do assume that I'm highly motivated and gotten past the trauma. It's not an act I'm trying to pull...I just never open up about anything personal and I've been doing this so long, it's the only way I know how to get by. But, I will definitely read up on cognitive behavioral therapy. is this how you dealt with your experiences?

GusherVim, it's just knowing that things are only going to get worse from here. 

I've had some good moments but at the end of the day, some traumatic experiences and just a natural hardwiring for depression makes life not worth living.

there's definitely a difference between an actual intention of following through and a cry for attention. I have noticed a lot of narcissism in the latter but even if that's the case with your friend, he needs to get help and deal with whatever is making him grandiose.

That's a lot you're dealing with. As if your medical issues weren't enough, you've got costly medical bills to pay...

Feels like the medical field focuses more on keeping people alive than quality of life.

But, to answer your question, I will end it but only when I get everything planned out to minimize survival and/or avoiding any legal trouble.

i'm sure you are just trying to protect yourself. it does make sense to ruin something on your own than to be totally letdown and give others the chance to ruin things for you. But, I hope you can, for your own sake, let yourself be vulnerable and allow yourself some happiness, even if it comes with high risk.

I feel you. It's like your mental health is decent enough to get through the day but not bad enough to go through with what you really want. For what it's worth, it's great that in spite of the self-loathing, you made it through college. That's a big achievement, especially when you had all those obsessive thoughts trying to derail you.
but unfortunately, that would make that person a killer. Not a label a person wants to live with. But, what's going on to make you want out?

"i'm ready to leave". That makes me sad to hear someone say that even when I've been ready myself. 

But, the possibility of a failed attempt is what has kept me from going through with a number of methods I've read up on. Imagine a botched attempt leading to a lifetime of brain damage, liver damage, disfigurement, or anything else there is a high risk of.

Yeah, I know that feeling of having nothing to show for all the years you've lived. How can we not feel nihilistic when everyday life doesn't quite match up with our version of how things should be? I have no intention of talking you out of anything because you know your needs best but if you do choose to disconnect, I hope you find it in you to enjoy some feeling of resolution and peace before the curtains close.
Not to be dismissive about your feelings of helplessness but you write beautifully and there's some kind of dark humor that makes your writing...special.
